subject: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@opsync.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the KV-caching example. We're kicking off a 3-month pilot to validate both throughput and cost savings for our search augmentation feature. Before procurement, we need clarity on packaging:

- Which plan would you recommend for a pilot expected to generate ~250k tokens/day with peaks to 600k/day?
- Can we mix a throughput-first bundle (reserved GPU for bursts) with a limited feature set (no dedicated observability add-on) and then swap to a full bundle if we hit the SLA?
- Any onboarding or pilot credits you can apply — procurement will ask for line-item discounts in the SOW.

Attached: Pilot_Specs.pdf (sample traffic, expected query distribution).

Ideal timeline: procurement needs a formal price/packaging note this week to start their internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sam Rivera
Head of Platform Integrations
Opsync

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@opsync.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear spec. Quick suggestions based on the traffic profile:

1) Pilot starter (recommended) — a capped Dedicated pool sized for 250k average / 600k burst. Includes:
   - Reserved throughput tier (burst pool)
   - Prefix/KV caching enabled
   - Basic Console dashboards (30d retention)
   - No dedicated observability add-on (saves ~15% on list price)

2) Throughput-first metered plan — lower upfront, higher per-token at peak; good if you want to avoid reserved commits.

3) Swap path: we can stage a canary rollback policy so the pilot runs on the starter bundle and automatically rolls to the full bundle (observability + extended logs) when you hit 75% of burst capacity for 3 consecutive days.

On discounts: we typically offer a pilot onboarding credit or a one-time implementation credit rather than a recurring discount. For a 3-month pilot I can propose a one-time credit (12–15%) or a reduced onboarding fee if procurement needs a line item.

I've attached a compact pricing sheet for both options (Redwood_Pricing_Sheet.xlsx). If you can confirm target spend ceiling and whether procurement needs a line-item discount vs credit, I'll get a formal note over to procurement/legal.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs

Looping in a couple of operational points from pricing:

- If Opsync wants reserved burst capacity + no observability add-on, we can structure a "starter" SKU with a 3-month commit and a step-up option. Pricing note: 8% list reduction on the starter SKU if they commit to a 3-month reserved pool at minimum X GPU-hours.
- We can include a one-time onboarding credit (flat dollar credit applied at first invoice) rather than changing per-token rates. That keeps their list price intact for future negotiations.
- If procurement insists on an explicit discount line in the SOW, legal will want to see the concession documented as a conditional credit (e.g., $10k onboarding credit contingent on signed 3-month pilot).

Chloe — I left a placeholder in the pricing sheet for the exact GPU-hour threshold (we'll pick based on traffic).

—Ben
Principal Sales Ops

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@opsync.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs

Appreciate the fast follow. Procurement will prefer a line-item discount in the SOW (their template expects a % discount). If you're rigid on credits vs discounts we can escalate, but it slows approvals.

Concessions ask from our side:
- 20% one-time onboarding discount on list price OR $12k onboarding credit (we're flexible)
- 3-month pilot term; auto-convert to annual if we hit 60% of burst capacity for 30 days
- DocuSign-ready SOW by EOD Friday would be ideal.

Procurement contacts: procurement@opsync.com

Thanks,
Sam

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@opsync.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs

Sam — thanks, quick response:

We can meet procurement halfway to avoid delays. Proposed concession:

- Offer a 12% one-time onboarding credit (applied as a credit on the first invoice) AND a $5k implementation credit.
- Add an explicit SOW line that indicates the equivalent net concession for procurement reporting ("Onboarding concession equivalent to 17% of onboarding fees, applied as a first-invoice credit"). This satisfies their template without changing list prices on tokens/throughput.
- Pilot term: 3 months with an auto-convert clause if Opsync triggers the threshold (60% burst for 30 days). Conversion pricing will be the then-current list price; we can add a 90-day notice window for Opsync to opt into an annual commitment and preserve the pilot effective rate.

Next steps: I uploaded a short proposal doc to the shared drive (see link). Legal will need to sign off on the wording; Chloe, can you confirm the GPU-hour placeholder and I'll route to Contracts for a quick SOW draft.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@opsync.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for Opsync pilot — tier/feature tradeoffs

That sounds workable — procurement will accept the SOW language as an "equivalent concession". Please send the DocuSign link and the draft SOW; procurement will review and loop legal if needed. We're aiming to finalize by next Wednesday.

Best,
Sam
Procurement: procurement@opsync.com
